options.label: Energy partition model

applicable.reason: Energy partition splits total energy into kcal from each chosen nutrient and kcal from everything else, so every chosen nutrient must carry energy in a known unit. sugar carries no energy: no Atwater factor is known for it.

options.estimand: The effect of adding calories from the nutrient while calories from every other source are held fixed, which is an addition and not a substitution.

atwater_check.sentence: Declared energy reconstructs to 4·protein + 4·carbohydrate + 9·fat + 7·alcohol within 1% across 17,078 rows, so the units are internally consistent — kilocalories and grams. Every downstream step is a function of total energy, and a unit error there is invisible in the final tables.

adjuster_lineage.formula: kcal_from_protein = 4 × protein  (protein: 4 kcal per unit, as given for this column)
kcal_from_carb = 4 × carb  (carb is carbohydrate; the Atwater reconstruction on the fitting rows confirms grams, so 4 kcal/g)
kcal_from_fat_total = 9 × fat_total  (fat_total is fat; the Atwater reconstruction on the fitting rows confirms grams, so 9 kcal/g)

partition_on_macronutrient_totals.why_this_subset: Partition refuses the full nutrient set; this is the same method on the energy-bearing macronutrient totals (one column per Atwater role, the one with the largest mean).

findings.title: 'imputed_bmi' is already a true/false column
findings.detail: 'imputed_bmi' holds two values — 'True' (306 rows) and 'False' (21,543 rows). Its values are already true and false, so reading it as binary re-types the column to 1 and 0 rather than repairing anything.
findings.why_it_matters: Read as binary, True becomes 1 and False becomes 0, and the column keeps its meaning: a rate, an odds ratio and a class balance are all defined for it. Coercing it to a number instead gives the same digits with no statement of what 1 means.

findings.title: 'meds_chol' holds True/False values in a text column
findings.detail: 4,645 value(s), every one of them True or False, stored as text rather than as a yes/no column, with 17,204 blank.
findings.why_it_matters: Stored this way the column is neither a number nor a label. Modeling, correlation and feature selection all refuse it, and the error they raise reads 'Unknown label type: unknown … on a regression target with continuous values' — which blames the column for being continuous when the problem is how it is stored.

findings.title: Nutrient associations need energy adjustment
findings.detail: `kcal` is total energy, and 19 other numeric columns are candidate nutrients.
findings.why_it_matters: Every nutrient association is confounded by total intake — people who eat more of everything eat more of anything. That the adjustment is needed is not in dispute. The residual method is the default form because it decorrelates the nutrient from energy explicitly, which makes the resulting coefficient interpretable; nutrient density is offered beside it, and that choice is a convention rather than a fact.

evidence.source: research/NUTRITION_PACK.md#04 · Energy adjustment — the methodological signature

findings.title: 'gender' is a binary variable written as text
findings.detail: 'gender' holds two values — 'male' (10,654 rows) and 'female' (11,195 rows). It is a binary variable, not a number stored as text.
findings.why_it_matters: Read as binary, male becomes 1 and female becomes 0. Which level is the positive one is your call — nothing in the file says — and the direction of every coefficient for this variable follows from it.

findings.title: 501 records report an implausible daily intake
findings.detail: `kcal` is below 500 on 194 record(s) and above 5000 on 307. Observed range 0 to 15,594.
findings.why_it_matters: These are possible days and poor estimates: a recall of 300 kcal is under-reporting rather than starvation. Excluding them is an eligibility criterion, which changes N and is reported in participant flow — so it is offered here and never applied. Nothing is filtered unless you say so.
